session_covered: US and European sessions of Monday 12 October
intro: Covers the US session of Monday 12 October (US stocks open; Columbus Day, so the US Treasury market was closed). Official closing prints and Tuesday's SPI 200 reading were not published in any source reachable this morning; US index figures are late-session (~3pm ET) snapshots and are labelled as such.
footnotes: Iron ore (62% Fe, CFR China): the email gave "Iron ore (62% Fe, Singapore Nov futures) US$91.20/t (Mon afternoon) +0.7%".

US index figures are not official closes; S&P 500 and Nasdaq levels agree across Yahoo Finance and MarketScreener. Brent was quoted at US$103.46/bbl (-1.2%) in Asian afternoon trade per ABC, a different time and likely a different contract; the US-hours figure is shown. The iron ore figure is a Singapore futures price, not a CFR China print; Friday's quoted price was US$90.60/t. The 10-year yield is the Friday level of ~5.24% carried through the holiday.

setup.summary: SPI 200 / ASX 200 futures for Tuesday: not available (no second independent source; Tuesday morning wraps were not yet published). Implied open: not available. The ASX 200 closed Monday up 0.8% at 8,783 pts (All Ords +0.7% to 8,937). US tone was mixed (Dow up, Nasdaq and chips down, oil higher).

what_moved: Oil rose after deadly strikes on Riyadh's airport over the weekend, partly offset by Trump's announcement that Russia and Ukraine agreed to halt attacks on energy facilities. Intraday, energy (+1.4%), communication services (+1.1% to +1.5%) and financials (+0.7%) led; technology (-1.0%) lagged, with the Philadelphia semiconductor index down 2.7% to a three-week low. Investors are positioned ahead of bank earnings and US inflation data.

news.headline: Riyadh airport strike lifts oil.
news.summary: Houthi attacks on Riyadh's airport killed at least 12-13 people; Brent traded above US$106/bbl, near two-week highs.

news.headline: Russia-Ukraine energy truce and diesel deal.
news.summary: Trump said both sides agreed to halt attacks on energy facilities; a separate deal waives Russian diesel sanctions through April 2027. Zelenskiy has accused Russia of a violation.

news.headline: Rates stay in focus.
news.summary: Markets price about a 19% chance of a Fed hike this month; Treasury yields hit 24-year highs earlier in October.

news.headline: Chip sell-off.
news.summary: The Philadelphia semiconductor index fell 2.7% intraday amid AI-bubble concerns and Chinese memory-maker progress.

news.headline: Earnings season opens.
news.summary: JPMorgan, Goldman Sachs and Citi report Tuesday; S&P 500 Q3 earnings are expected to rise 30.6%.

news.headline: Hormuz.
news.summary: Tehran said it will respond to a US proposal on reopening the Strait of Hormuz after review.

news.headline: Telco shares fall globally.
news.summary: Reports of SpaceX buying spectrum hit telcos; Telstra fell 2.5% as the ASX 200 still rose 0.8%.

news.headline: US consumer sentiment weakens.
news.summary: The index fell to a five-month low of 46.3.

coming_up: US September CPI on Wednesday 14 October (US time) is the week's key release; PPI follows on Thursday 15 October.
